html:
The Barindji, also written Parrintyi, are an Aboriginal Australian people of western New South Wales. Their country lay on the dry plains east of the lower Darling River.

They should not be confused with the Paaruntyi to the north, who spoke a similar language but whom the Barindji called "the spitting people". Their neighbours included the Barkindji of the river and the Yitha Yitha to the south. Little more is recorded. Sheep stations spread over this country from the 1850s and 1860s.
